reading.title: Body Systems 1: an anatomy teaching session
reading.text: A trainer uses a muscle model. The biceps helps bend the elbow, the triceps helps straighten it, and the quadriceps helps straighten the knee. These muscles contract to produce movement. A biology tutor identifies the hamstrings at the back of the thigh, calf muscles at the back of the lower leg, abdominal muscles at the front of the trunk, and deltoids around the shoulders. The class compares muscles with immune structures. Gluteal muscles move the hip, and pectoral muscles are in the chest. White blood cells help defend the body, and antibodies are proteins involved in immune responses. The tutor explains that an antigen can trigger an immune response. Lymph nodes contain immune cells and filter lymph. Tonsils are areas of immune tissue near the back of the throat. The tutor explains that bicep and tricep are common informal forms of the anatomical names biceps and triceps. A calf muscle helps move the ankle, and a deltoid helps move the shoulder. A gluteus is a buttock muscle involved in hip movement. A white blood cell is an immune cell, while a tonsil is a group of immune tissues near the back of the throat.

Anatomically accurate manufactured teaching models only; no gore, exposed patient anatomy, diagnosis, treatment steps, readable labels, arrows, logos, or answer highlighting.
